charterSection: Release B — receptions; A4 metric appropriateness
finding: player_receptions coverage 0.8845 breached the [0.72, 0.88] band by 0.0045. Diagnosis on the champion's per-point dump: 25.4% of actual outcomes land EXACTLY on an interval endpoint (median interval width 4.1 catches; strict coverage 0.630, inclusive 0.884). An inclusive interval over a small-integer count CANNOT hit nominal 80% — endpoint probability masses are indivisible — so the continuous-variable coverage contract is statistically inappropriate for count families. This is a measurement-definition defect, not a model defect and not a threshold to shave.

amendment.rule: For integer-count families (player_receptions is currently the only one), interval coverage is scored MID-P: an outcome strictly inside counts 1, an outcome equal to either endpoint counts 1/2. Continuous families are unchanged. Quantiles, pinball, MAE and ECE are unchanged everywhere.
amendment.whyMidP: the standard discrete-coverage treatment: splits the indivisible endpoint mass instead of awarding or denying all of it, making the nominal level attainable in expectation.
amendment.prospective: This amendment does NOT retroactively re-grade the existing receipt. It applies from the next receipt generated under it; that re-receipt is a fresh evaluation event whose outcome is not pinned here — receptions may land PUBLIC or stay SHADOW wherever the amended measurement puts it (all other bars unchanged: ece <= 0.05, beats both baselines, n >= 300).

alsoRecorded.rushing: coverage/calibration failure is structured: high-opportunity backs (>=12 carries) run cov 0.645 with a +27.4-yd under-predicted center (share-dilution, the QB mechanism on lead backs) while low-opportunity backs are in band (0.812). Named future candidate: train-fit share-conditional center correction. NOT run in this program; rushing stays withheld.

notes: Registered before the amended measurement was implemented or any re-receipt ran; commit order is the proof.
